summary.intent: Implement issue #618 (core det-CBOR codec + KAT test-vector spine) while orchestrating parallel background agents for independent v2-build issues (#624 API auth, #623 engine scaffold, #645 Tauri shell), then run a crypto/privacy security review on the resulting PR and remediate findings.
summary.outcome: #618 landed as PR #659 with the 'Core KATs (native + WASM)' check registered as required on main; standards/spec reviews and a follow-up crypto-privacy-review surfaced real bugs (error Display truncation, missing encode-side depth guard, generator header loophole, CI freshness/path-filter gaps) which were fixed and force-pushed. #624 and #645 completed in isolated worktrees awaiting human review; #623 was still running at session end. The crypto-privacy-review skill's output-contract (writing/committing reports under .planning/security/) was corrected to use a scratchpad instead.

repo: crates/core/src must stay pure (no I/O/clock/RNG) — kat_gen.rs is an example binary and is exempt from this rule

Codec error surface is split into two disjoint classes, trust vs malformed, each with uniquely named checks in error.rs; the boundary (e.g. tags/floats/oversize-simple-values = malformed) is a frozen judgement call requiring explicit human sign-off since re-classing later breaks committed KAT vectors

kat_gen.rs is the sole intended writer of crates/core/kat/manifest.json — it was found preserving manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the existing file on regen, letting hand-edits silently survive the CI freshness diff; fixed to hardcode/own every manifest byte
The 'rust' CI path filter did not include .cargo/config.toml, so changes to the wasm runner config could skip the core-kats job
proptest's fork feature (needed for wait-timeout) does not build under wasm32-wasip1; Cargo.toml must split the proptest dev-dependency forkless-per-target for the wasm leg
Half-float bit pattern f90014 aliased `false` under naive dispatch — decoder dispatch must key on CBOR additional-info, not just major-type-derived guesses
apps/api convention: revoke = hard DELETE, never a soft-revoked flag
apps/api vitest must compile through SWC (unplugin-swc) because esbuild can't emit decorator metadata Nest needs; dev/CLI scripts must run via ts-node, not tsx, or Nest DI silently breaks

SIWE in this repo is link-then-login only (no implicit account creation) — a bare wallet signature can't prove possession of an identity publicKey, so allowing SIWE-first account creation would enable squatting a victim's publicKey

The crypto-privacy-review skill file (.claude/commands/crypto-privacy-review.md) is repo-tracked and previously specified writing/committing its report under .planning/security/ on the feature branch — corrected to a scratchpad path so review artifacts don't ride along in PRs

code.finding: build_manifest previously preserved manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the on-disk file rather than generating them, allowing hand-edits to survive the freshness check; fixed to own all manifest fields
Display impl for a malformed-key error truncated output; also documents the frozen trust-vs-malformed classification rationale added after review
Encoder was missing a depth guard symmetric to the decoder's MAX_DEPTH=128 check; added during crypto-privacy-review fixes
rust path filter missing .cargo/config.toml (fixed); freshness-check step also had an untracked-file blind spot (fixed separately during crypto review)
proptest dev-dependency split by target so the fork feature (unsupported on wasm32-wasip1) only applies natively

workflow: Launching independent GitHub issues as background agents in isolated git worktrees lets unrelated slices (#624, #623, #645) progress in parallel with interactive work on #618
Before trusting a worktree agent's self-report, verify its branch/commits directly on disk (git log/status) rather than taking the summary at face value
Cross-referencing each open issue's 'Depends on:' line against in-flight work is an effective way to find genuinely parallelizable next slices

Running two independent review agents (Standards axis, Spec axis) over a diff before opening a PR caught real bugs (manifest header loophole, unregistered required CI check) that a single reviewer might have missed

A dedicated crypto-privacy-review pass after merge-readiness caught additional issues (Display truncation, missing encode-side depth guard) that the earlier standards/spec review passes didn't surface

friction: proptest's fork feature failed to build under wasm32-wasip1, requiring a target-conditional Cargo.toml split before the wasm test leg would pass
kat_gen's manifest-preservation behavior undermined the 'committed generator is the only writer' guarantee — required a follow-up fix after two independent reviewers flagged it

The crypto-privacy-review skill's built-in process wrote and committed its report onto the working branch under .planning/security/, which had to be walked back (report moved to scratchpad, commit dropped from the branch) and the skill file itself edited to fix the contract
Greptile PR comments on #659 surfaced mid-session but were explicitly deferred ('pick up ... right after these fixes land') rather than addressed immediately
